clue.text: Fatty's middle hurt getting fastened

indicators.note: the middle of Fatty's means the word with its first and last letters stripped away

parts.note: hurt in the sense of felt pain, ached

explanation.surface: An overweight person's sore belly is somehow linked to being strapped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' takes all but the outside letters of FATTY, leaving ATT; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attached is joined or secured to something else, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Reject ruling, a heartless order to imprison bishop

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding within, so one piece goes inside
heartless means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: to order is to dictate
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A ruler rejects a ruling ordering a bishop jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the central letter of the order; the bishop then sits right after the A. 'Reject ruling' means renounce the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce the throne, giving up the right to rule.

clue.text: Bolshie workers fast surrounding policemen

indicators.note: surrounding tells us the other pieces go round the police force

parts.note: TU is a trade union, a body of workers
RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Striking workers ring police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: RUC goes between T and U. 'Bolshie' is British slang for awkward and rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent means aggressively defiant, matching the British slang word for stroppy.

clue.text: Conservative has joined opponents for division

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the UK political party
the left are the political opponents of the Conservatives

explanation.surface: A Tory crosses the floor, creating a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has joined' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure dividing something.

clue.text: Serious attention given to snug home

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
a nest is a cosy home

explanation.surface: Grave care devoted to a cosy house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is sincere and serious.

clue.text: Start to flourish in a reasonable business

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a reasonable price or deal is a fair one

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, here the opening of flourish

explanation.surface: Advice on how a sensible company might begin to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of 'flourish' goes inside A FAIR, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean a matter or concern, as in 'that is my business'.

clue.text: Prevent everything being covered by trees

indicators.note: in a down clue, being covered by means placed beneath the other piece

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
everything is all

explanation.surface: The whole land is under woodland cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being covered by' works because this is a down entry: the second piece sits beneath the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act first to stop something from happening.

clue.text: Family man's partner is cheerfully confident after discarding jack

indicators.note: discarding means throwing away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: jaunty means breezy and self-assured
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A relative's spouse cheers up after losing a card.
explanation.walkthrough: The family man is an uncle; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle's wife is an aunt, here in its informal spelling.

clue.text: Joint appeal about drug

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to refer a matter is to appeal to someone for a decision
E is slang for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A plea is made on a narcotics case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' sounds like a body part or a connection but is slang for a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a cannabis cigarette, also slangily called a joint.

clue.text: One pondering about old cat

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: one who muses or ponders is a muser

explanation.surface: A thinker reflects on an elderly cat.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside MUSER after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat valued for catching mice, so a specific kind of cat.

clue.text: Put out some medicine you said should be swallowed

indicators.note: being swallowed means taken inside, so the letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: a measured amount of medicine is a dose

indicators.note: said tells us to use the letter that is pronounced like the spoken word you

parts.note: the word you is pronounced like the letter U

explanation.surface: A nurse tells a patient to take their pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'give out medicine' but means extinguish.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse a fire is to put it out by drenching it with water.

clue.text: Ordering a new flower border

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions to a gardener to plant fresh edging around the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river; the Rio Grande forms part of the border between the USA and Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: This river marks much of the frontier between Texas and Mexico, so it is a border formed by flowing water.

clue.text: Lady hoards money in huge quantities

indicators.note: hoards means keeps something stored within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a countess is a titled lady, wife of an earl
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: An aristocratic woman stockpiles vast amounts of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a pound sterling comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that cannot be counted are innumerable, existing in vast numbers.

clue.text: Old writer's personal mannerisms

definitions.meaning: an old writing implement, a stylus for marking wax tablets, was once called by this name
a person's characteristic manner of doing or expressing things

explanation.surface: A dead author had distinctive habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'writer' is not an author but a pointed instrument; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic name for a stylus, and also a distinctive manner of expression.

clue.text: Risk having to accept surcharge finally on that account

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a risk or danger is a threat

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word surcharge, its closing letter

explanation.surface: A customer faces danger by putting up with an extra fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on that account' is an archaic phrase; 'having to accept' puts the fee's last letter inside the danger word.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning for that reason or because of it.

clue.text: Mention a rewritten article included in issue

indicators.note: included in tells us one piece is put inside the rearranged letters
rewritten means the words are recomposed into a new order

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor revises a piece and slips in a feature for the next number.
explanation.walkthrough: MENTION A is rearranged and a second A, the article, is placed among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows or comes out, as to issue is to come forth.

clue.text: About a couple of lines, introduction to yours truly

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter, here the start of yours

explanation.surface: A note about a short letter signed off 'yours truly'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' reads as a sign-off, but 'truly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning genuinely or in fact.

clue.text: Extremely stupid, at any rate

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., the very opposite of clever
a dated adverb meaning at least or in any case

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is very dim, anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'least wise', the answer reads as the most foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adverb meaning at least or in any case.

clue.text: Knowing parts of Crete have been captured in camera

indicators.note: being captured means held inside another piece

parts.note: knowing as in artful or cunning, sly

indicators.note: parts of tells us the word is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Spies captured in Crete were photographed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' breaks up the island's name before it is captured. 'in camera' is legal Latin for in private, not photography.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase meaning in private, away from the public.

clue.text: Sound, just sound

indicators.note: the second sound tells us to use a word pronounced like the honest-sounding synonym

parts.note: just in the sense of honest and fair, straight

explanation.surface: A verdict on an argument: solid and fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Sound' is a noun, a narrow channel of sea; the second is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of sea between two land masses, a synonym.

clue.text: Not quite the finest place in Egypt

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: the finest means the best

explanation.surface: A traveller reckons a city on the Nile is nearly the top spot.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BEST loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great ancient city on the Nile in Upper Egypt.

clue.text: Farming only while young?

definitions.meaning: the working and cultivating of land for crops
read as two words: lasting just until a person gets old

explanation.surface: Agriculture is something you do in your youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into 'till age', a whimsical reading signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the preparation of land for growing crops, an agricultural term.

clue.text: Roman historian sends bill in to Emperor

indicators.note: sending one thing in to another means putting it inside

parts.note: Titus was a Roman emperor
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A writer sends an invoice to the ruler of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends ... in to' is the container signal, split around the bill; 'sends' carries no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian who wrote the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Primate left after church service

indicators.note: after tells us the ape and left come behind the church

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey departs once the church service is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop in a churchy clue, but it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapel is a religious service, as in a school where pupils attend daily worship.

clue.text: Young person losing head to a girl

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a young person is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster loses their head over a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILD without its first letter is HILD; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilda is a female first name, as girl stands for any woman's name in crosswords.

clue.text: Threateningly approaches textile machinery

definitions.meaning: rises up in a menacing way, as a storm does
devices for weaving thread into cloth

explanation.surface: Weaving machines bearing down menacingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning appears menacingly, and the plural of the weaving machine.

clue.text: Meeting points in front of bar

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
a bar in a pub or shop is a counter

explanation.surface: People gather at spots by the front of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' says the points come before the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, often an unexpected one.

clue.text: Some amount I left in till

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cashier leaves part of the takings in the cash drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'in till' was wrong: 'in' is a link word and 'till' alone means the same as the answer. 'till' looks like a cash drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: Till is a shortened form meaning up to the time that.

clue.text: Turn out books I'd held, being careful with money

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to turn out a certain way is to prove so
taken as written without the apostrophe
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone empties out books they had kept, being thrifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts I'D inside the verb; 'being' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A provident person plans ahead and is thrifty, a synonym.

clue.text: Misrepresent poor orphan

definitions.meaning: to distort or bend the truth of something
Oliver, the poor orphan of Dickens's novel, bears this surname

explanation.surface: A distorted account of an unhappy foundling.
explanation.walkthrough: The orphan is Oliver in Charles Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent words is to distort them; also the surname of Dickens's famous workhouse boy.

clue.text: In record, offence likely to go down

indicators.note: In at the start places the offence within the record

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A crime on file means a probable conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go down' suggests going to prison but here means being defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A losing team or bet is one destined to fail or be beaten.

clue.text: Ordered spy's cover to change — a plucky old thing?

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
ordered means put into a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
to change is to alter

explanation.surface: A spy is told to switch identities, asking if this brave old hand can manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reworks the spy into PSY, which goes round the change; 'to' is a link word. 'plucky' means brave on the surface but here means plucked.
explanation.definitionFit: The psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument played by plucking.
